threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'crossing the road' instead of 'jumping the zebra' when you're near the station. The locals know it’s all about the timing and the right gap!
Caught a guy on the 196 who kept insisting that the moon was following us. Said it was a sign. Had the whole back row cracking up.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a kid trading Pokémon cards in Turkish at the playground—realized the old and new were perfectly blended here.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Döner shop open at 3 AM serving currywurst with a side of techno beats from the club next door. Truly unique.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they’re from here if they know not to trust the 49 bus schedule on weekends. It’s like, why even check?

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 14 Mission and watched a guy try selling homemade tamales to bored passengers. A classic Muni moment—where else do you get lunch and street art on wheels?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'Gràcia' only means Gaudí. They miss the real life buzzing in the squares, the hidden bars with no signs, and that secret vibe we cherish.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their shoes—if they're still sporting white sneakers, they haven't yet learned the cobbles will wreck them.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still pronounce it 'Hack-knee' instead of 'Hack-nee'. The locals don't let that slide, trust me.
Last night on the 333, two blokes argued over which was worse, last week's tube strike or their exes. You could cut the tension with a knife.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I realized I was home? Hearing a toddler serenade the street with his ukulele while an old man danced along on Wutzkyallee.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, you can find spontaneous street art battles every weekend. Crews roll out, spray cans in hand, competing for the most jaw-dropping piece.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their reaction to the smell of sourdough at Tartine—it's a nostalgic smile, not just hunger.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a dinosaur costume on the 49 bus, totally unphased by the chaos around him. Just another day in the Tenderloin, I guess.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists miss how locals actually avoid Passeig de Gràcia for shopping; we prefer the hidden boutiques in Carrer de Verdi for unique finds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always spot them by their constant Google Maps checks, even in Diagonal's leafy streets—like they’ve never seen a grid before.
